learning_objective.evidence: “A budget administrator should not be able to export detailed billing data. Which design expresses that?” tests this identifiable IAM/export boundary: Separate budget-management permissions from billing-export and BigQuery dataset permissions.

prompt_quality.evidence: The complete prompt “A budget administrator should not be able to export detailed billing data. Which design expresses that?” identifies a bounded principal, operation or resource-scope condition and asks for the next permission design/diagnosis.

technical_correctness.evidence: The key “Separate budget-management permissions from export and dataset permissions” is consistent with current Google Cloud role and data-access documentation: Separate budget-management permissions from billing-export and BigQuery dataset permissions.

answer_scoring_contract.evidence: choice_single/exact_selected_set scores only A (“Separate budget-management permissions from export and dataset permissions”); it matches the requested single authorization principle or diagnosis, with no partial credit, aliases, or hidden accepted values.

distractor_quality.evidence: Individually assessed exact active wrong choices: B “Grant both capabilities through Owner”; C “Use a VM service account for the analyst”; D “Grant organization-wide Viewer”. reason.evidence: Reason: “Budget and export operations are independent capabilities.” It names the billing/data/resource boundary needed for this specific question.

details.evidence: The boundary/mechanism text is generally aligned to Separate budget-management permissions from billing-export and BigQuery dataset permissions., but the source URL is https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/export-data-bigquery-setup and does not directly document this item’s exact IAM operation. The export setup page explains configuring export, not this distinct IAM investigation/least-privilege principle.

wrong_option_explanations.evidence: B/C/D messages use the repeated form “This choice would cross the stated billing boundary because it would …”; e.g. B “This choice would cross the stated billing boundary because it would grant both capabilities through Owner.”.
